text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The new Selangor chief minister to replace Muhammad Muhammad Taib who resigned on April 14 is expected to be announced today. Muhammad Taib quit amid a probe into undeclared cash he was carrying while departing from Australia.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad arrived on Thursday in Malawi for a three-day official visit, the first leg of his weeklong tour of three African countries.
-- Workers' Day was celebrated on a very subdued scale this year, reflecting what seems to be waning interest in the trade union movement.
-- UMNO Youth says the quota system for economic and education sectors will have to be reviewed to provide equal opportunities to all Malaysians by the year 2020.
-- Trade among the ASEAN-7, already the fastest growing intra-subregional trade in Asia and the Pacific, is likely to accelerate when Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos are admitted as members this year.

-- Fourteen African heads of state, along with Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, are expected to take part in a unique five-day southern African economic conference opening Saturday outside a game reserve in northern Botswana.
